subject: Re: Annual prepay — proposal for surge handling and onboarding accelerator
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@acmehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Switching to annual prepay — need pricing + spike protection

Hi Alex,

Quick context: Acme Health is currently on monthly billing (~$85k/month running inference for a set of clinical NLP workloads). We're evaluating switching to an annual prepay to simplify procurement and get better unit economics. Two asks from my side before I loop procurement/legal:

1) What material term discounts do you offer for a 12-month prepay vs a 24-month prepay?
2) We have regular seasonal spikes (up to ~35% above baseline) — how do you handle burst capacity and pricing for overage?
3) Any onboarding credits or ramp protections if our usage ramps slowly in the first 3–6 months?

I can share an estimate of our expected token ramp if that helps. We prefer a single annual invoice and a simple true-up cadence.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call tomorrow if needed.

—Samir
Samir Rao
Head of AI Platforms, Acme Health
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Switching to annual prepay — need pricing + spike protection

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear asks. High-level proposal below (happy to refine against the ramp numbers you mentioned):

Proposal (12-month prepay) — baseline:
- Term discount: 18% off list token pricing for annual prepay (applies to committed volume).
- Monthly true-up: monthly reconciliation against committed baseline, with any overage billed at list rate unless covered by surge cap.
- Surge handling: built-in surge cap of 30% above committed throughput, covered by the prepay at the discounted rate; bursts beyond the cap billed at list + 25% ad-hoc premium.
- Onboarding accelerator: one-time credit of $25,000 applied across first two months to offset integration/overage risk.
- Ramp protection: 3-month soft ramp floor at 60% of committed baseline for true-up calculations (protects you from early underutilization).
- KPIs: Latency 95th percentile SLA (we can define thresholds) — performance rebate up to 1% of monthly spend if SLA missed more than twice in a quarter.

Alternative (24-month prepay) — optional:
- Term discount: 22% off list token pricing for a 24-month committed prepay.
- Larger onboarding accelerator: $35,000 applied in month 1–3.
- Surge cap: 40% included; ad-hoc overflow supported at list + 20% (pre-approved by us).

Attachments: I attached a drafted SOW and a pricing matrix (spreadsheet) to show worked examples against a few ramp scenarios. Also linking our standard prepay T&Cs: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/SOW-Acme-2026

If you want to pursue 24-months, we can discuss a step-down true-up schedule (e.g., 6/9/12 month checkpoints) instead of monthly reconciliation to ease your finance operations.

If this looks directionally good, I can route a redlined SOW to your procurement for review and loop in our finance lead.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Switching to annual prepay — need pricing + spike protection

Alex — thanks for the quick response and the materials. A few points from procurement/legal that need clarification before we push to signatures: 

Thanks for the proposal — couple clarifying Qs:
- We were expecting deeper term economics for a strategic multi-year engagement. Would Redwood consider a better rate for a 24-month guarantee (we were targeting ~25–28% off list)?
- Can you provide a concrete ramp schedule example (month-by-month expected consumption ranges) and how credits apply if we miss ramp targets? Our budget team wants clear examples for the monthly true-up.
- The surge cap language is good; we want to confirm whether surge capacity is prioritized or best-effort when your fleet is constrained (we need guaranteed burst for critical job windows).

Also, our legal wants your standard data processing addendum and evidence of SOC 2 controls. Please send those and flag any clauses in your SOW that are non-negotiable.

If possible, please include an example payment schedule (single annual invoice vs monthly true-up) and what the onboarding accelerator offsets (credits vs service fees).

—Procurement (on behalf of Samir)
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme Health — procurement asks (pricing + surge guarantees)

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement note (below). They pushed back on discount depth and want concrete ramp examples + guaranteed surge for critical windows. Pricing summary I shared is in the attached pricing-matrix-20260921.xlsx.

Request: can we offer an escalated concession to close on a 24-month? I'm proposing we consider: 
- 22% term discount for 24-months (we might need approval for >22%).
- Increase included surge cap to 45% for the first 12 months, then step down to 30% thereafter.
- Increase onboarding accelerator to $40k (re-allocatable as credit against month 1–3 usage).

Trade: require finance to sign a 60% minimum committed baseline for months 1–6 (hard ramp floor) and a monthly true-up cadence. Also propose adding a short SLA credit (1.5% monthly credit) if latency SLA missed more than once in a quarter.

Ben/LA — can you confirm if finance approves the $40k accelerator and the 45% surge cap for Q1 acceptance? If not, what's the maximum concession window we can approve from sales?

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Final offer: 24-month prepay (accelerator & burst guarantees)

Samir / Procurement team — thanks for the back-and-forth and the clear asks. Based on internal approvals here is the consolidated offer we can put on the table: 

Consolidated commercial offer (24-month prepay):
- Term discount: 20% off list token pricing applied to committed annual volume.
- Onboarding accelerator: $40,000 credit applied against consumption in months 1–3 (appears on first invoice as a credit line).
- Surge capacity: included surge cap of 40% above committed baseline. For critical, pre-scheduled windows we will provide an increased overflow allowance of 50% (must be scheduled 48+ hours ahead and is guaranteed). Ad-hoc bursts beyond the included cap will be billed at list + 20%.
- Ramp protection & true-up: monthly true-up with a 6-month ramp floor at 60% of baseline for purposes of true-up billing. After month 6, normal reconciliation applies.
- Payment: single annual invoice issued at contract start (prepay). Monthly true-up will only adjust internal reporting; no additional invoice will be issued unless usage exceeds prepay and ad-hoc overflow is consumed.
- SLA & rebates: 95th pctl latency SLA; if breached more than once in a quarter, we will issue a 1% monthly credit against that month's prepay spend (up to 3% max per quarter).
- Legal/compliance: attached our SOC 2 summary and standard DPA. Any non-standard SOW clauses need to be flagged by your legal team; we can negotiate up to two customer-specific redlines before exec review.

Attached: redlined SOW (placeholder), pricing matrix with 3 ramp scenarios, SOC 2 summary.

Next steps:
1) If this is acceptable, procurement can confirm via email and we'll route final SOW + order form for signature.
2) Once signed, finance will issue a single annual invoice and our onboarding team will schedule a kickoff to capture ramp targets.

Happy to hop on a call early next week to walk through the payment terms and the surge scheduling process.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
